ATimeofWarIntro.2.full: My father was a genius! I state this now, not with the naïveté of my initial discovery of his journal, but as a time-tested statement of truth. It is why I pen these words today for posterity and to affirm with deep conviction what some may erroneously refer to as mad science.
ATimeofWarIntro.2.easy: My father was a genius! I say this now, not with the innocence I had when I first found his journal, but as a truth that has passed the test of time. That is why I write these words today, for the future, and to say with deep belief that this is not what some people wrongly call mad science.
ATimeofWarIntro.2.short: My father was a genius! I say it now not with the naïveté of first discovering his journal, but as tested truth, and write it for posterity against those who call it mad science.

ATimeofWarIntro.3.full: When I first arrived at my father's manor, I carried the same skepticism any normal individual would. Weary as I was from the excursion across the Hungarian plains, the cold, gray walls of the villa with its oppressive iron gates chilled me to my marrow. When the disfigured caretaker — the only person privileged with the knowledge — revealed to me a false door and spiraling staircase that descended to a secret laboratory, the grim discovery did nothing to soothe my nerves. In fact, the sight of jars filled with preserved flesh and the astringent stench of chemicals aggravated my frail state, leaving me to take my suppers in the bedroom for several weeks.
ATimeofWarIntro.3.easy: When I first arrived at my father's big house, I did not believe in any of it, like any normal person. I was tired from the trip across the Hungarian plains, and the cold, gray walls of the house with its heavy iron gates made me cold to the bone. The caretaker, whose face was badly damaged, was the only person who knew the secret. He showed me a hidden door and a spiral staircase that went down to a secret laboratory. This dark discovery did not calm my nerves at all. In fact, the jars full of preserved flesh and the sharp smell of chemicals made my weak health worse, and I ate my dinners in my bedroom for several weeks.
ATimeofWarIntro.3.short: Arriving at my father's manor, I was as skeptical as anyone. The cold villa chilled me, and when the disfigured caretaker showed me a hidden staircase to a secret laboratory full of preserved flesh and chemical stench, I took to my bedroom for weeks.

ATimeofWarIntro.4.full: But, it was this same dark discovery that eventually roused me from my illness. For as I pored over the journal bequeathed to me and surveyed page after page of formulaic experimentation, my apprehensions melted. I felt trepidacious, yet unreservedly enthusiastic at the ethical implications of this great task!
ATimeofWarIntro.4.easy: But it was this same dark discovery that finally woke me from my illness. As I read the journal he had left me, page after page of formulas and experiments, my worries melted away. I was nervous, but I also felt great excitement about what this important work meant for right and wrong!
ATimeofWarIntro.4.short: Yet that same discovery roused me. Poring over the journal's experiments, my fears melted into wholehearted enthusiasm for this great task!

ATimeofWarIntro.5.full: Yet even after the disquiet within my soul was relieved, the nearby village rattled my window panes with cacophonous revelry. At first, I kept my visits to the borough brief and infrequent. It seemed that whenever I turned my head I would lock eyes with a cautious observer, and I felt the entire town's steel gaze like daggers tickling the back of my skull. I could only speculate that my siblings endured the same sordid treatment.
ATimeofWarIntro.5.easy: But even after my soul was calm again, the village nearby shook my windows with its loud celebrations. At first, my visits to the town were short and not very often. It seemed that every time I turned my head, my eyes met the eyes of someone watching me carefully, and I felt the hard looks of the whole town like knives touching the back of my head. I could only guess that my brothers and sisters were treated in the same unpleasant way.
ATimeofWarIntro.5.short: But the village's noisy revelry rattled my windows. I kept my visits brief; wherever I turned, wary eyes met mine like daggers at my neck. I suspect my siblings fared no better.

ATimeofWarIntro.6.full: It was my spouse, using my extended rest to become better acquainted with the village, who explained how spirited political discourse was the source of this commotion. Then I could discern the rally cry of their evening demonstrations as they spoke of disobedience, the end of monarchy, and civil war.
ATimeofWarIntro.6.easy: My spouse used my long rest to get to know the village better, and explained to me that lively political discussions were the reason for all this noise. Then I could understand the cries of their evening protests, when they spoke of disobedience, the end of the king's rule, and civil war.
ATimeofWarIntro.6.short: My spouse, exploring the village while I rested, explained the cause: politics. Now I heard their nightly cries of disobedience, the end of the monarchy, and civil war.

ATimeofWarIntro.7.full: I began to realize the potential boon that war could provide for my research. If the people shared a mere fraction of the passion that now stoked the fires of my heart, how easily they would embrace my scientific assistance! While my father's ambitions were strong, his solitary existence had doomed his ideas to obscurity.
ATimeofWarIntro.7.easy: I started to understand how useful a war could be for my research. If the people had even a small part of the passion that now burned in my heart, how easily they would accept my scientific help! My father had great ambitions, but because he lived alone, nobody ever knew about his ideas.
ATimeofWarIntro.7.short: I began to see what war could do for my research. If the people shared even a fraction of my passion, they would gladly accept my science! My father's solitude had doomed his ideas to obscurity.

ATimeofWarIntro.8.full: I would not repeat this error. I would brave the jeers of the populace to guide them in the art of warfare. My efforts would determine the course of this conflict. And when the time comes, it will be my science that will emerge from the flames of war as the true victor!
ATimeofWarIntro.8.easy: I would not make this mistake again. I would be brave and accept the people laughing at me, to teach them the art of war. My work would decide how this conflict goes. And when the time comes, it will be my science that comes out of the flames of war as the real winner!
ATimeofWarIntro.8.short: I would not repeat his error. I would brave the people's jeers to guide them in war, and my science would emerge from its flames the true victor!

TimeTravelintro.2.full: Words failed to capture the scope of my sorrow. War, in all its awful beauty had befallen the once handsome province.
TimeTravelintro.2.easy: No words could describe how sad I was. War, with all its terrible beauty, had come to the once beautiful province.

TimeTravelintro.3.full: May my eyes never gaze upon another site so desolate and horrible as the scorched landscape left in ruin by the indifference of conflict. My blood ran cold, as if buried in this tainted, upturned soil. It felt as if my heart - like the rusted hinge of a coffin - had swung shut, steeling itself from the bleak, harsh world around me.
TimeTravelintro.3.easy: I hope my eyes never see another place as empty and horrible as this burned land, destroyed by a war that did not care. My blood went cold, as if it were buried in this poisoned, broken earth. It felt as if my heart, like the rusty hinge of a coffin, had closed to protect itself from the dark, hard world around me.
TimeTravelintro.3.short: May I never again see a land so scorched and ruined by war. My blood ran cold, and my heart swung shut like a rusted coffin lid against the bleak world.

TimeEnd2.3.full: Though my years have advanced and my vigor has left me, it is my hope that this final act will ensure the lustrous future which war had wrenched from me so long ago. Once more I venture into this box so my eyes will witness what I have wrought. Whether it is my coffin or my ship to sail amongst the cosmos, I welcome what fate lies in store for me.
TimeEnd2.3.easy: I am older now and my strength has left me, but I hope that this last act will make sure of the bright future that war took from me so long ago. Once more I go into this box, so that my eyes can see what I have done. Whether it is my coffin or my ship to sail through the stars, I welcome whatever fate has planned for me.
TimeEnd2.3.short: Old and weakened, I hope this final act restores the future war stole from me. Once more I step into the box. Coffin or ship to the stars, I welcome my fate.

ParadoxIntro.3.full: While the discovery of my family's experiments and journals would cement my scientific ambitions for years to come, I had never actually met them. I was too young to remember the disappearance of my brilliant progenitor. To lose a parent and then another to the subsequent dementia that followed was more folly than one child should ever have to bear. I was shielded from this reality, rushed away to Vienna, where I was consumed by my studies until my twenty-first year. It was only at my partner's insistence that I decided to settle my inheritance.
ParadoxIntro.3.easy: Finding my family's experiments and journals would decide my scientific plans for many years, but I had never really met them. I was too young to remember when my brilliant ancestor disappeared. Losing one parent, and then the other to the madness that followed, was more than one child should ever have to carry. They protected me from this truth and sent me quickly to Vienna, where I was busy with my studies until I was twenty-one. Only because my partner insisted did I decide to take care of my inheritance.
ParadoxIntro.3.short: My family's journals would shape my ambitions, yet I never knew them. I was too young to remember my brilliant progenitor's disappearance, or the dementia that took my other parent. Sheltered in Vienna until twenty-one, I came to settle my inheritance only at my partner's insistence.

ParadoxIntro.4.full: I remember being stunned as I arrived by train on a mid-summer's evening. I do not know what I expected from the anecdotes my nanny had relayed to me, but it  was not the bustling cityscape that greeted me. As the sun dipped into the forest, the glimmer of modern steel light fixtures amplified the urban luminescence. My delighted spouse and I enjoyed a quiet ride in our steamer car, which offered us a chance to observe the idyllic community and decidedly pleasant folk enjoying the convenience of electricity and steam turbine technology.
ParadoxIntro.4.easy: I remember how surprised I was when I arrived by train on an evening in the middle of summer. I do not know what I expected from the stories my nanny had told me, but it was not the busy city that welcomed me. As the sun went down behind the forest, the shine of modern steel lamps made the city lights even brighter. My happy spouse and I enjoyed a quiet ride in our steam car, which gave us a chance to see the perfect community and the very friendly people, who enjoyed the comfort of electricity and steam machines.
ParadoxIntro.4.short: Arriving by train on a midsummer evening, I was stunned: not the village of my nanny's tales, but a bustling, modern town glowing with steel lamps. From our steamer car, my spouse and I admired the pleasant folk enjoying electricity and steam.

ParadoxIntro.5.full: The estate appeared untouched by years of vacancy; recently pruned brambles and ivy adorned the iron gate and the expansive grounds were immaculate. A caretaker of great age and a small housekeeping staff greeted us. Although updating the grounds to the more modern standard of the nearby town would prove a daunting task, the servants’ warm reception allayed our remaining anxieties. Upon discovery of my family's laboratory, what had been planned as a mere visit received an indefinite extension.
ParadoxIntro.5.easy: The house looked as if all the years without anyone living in it had not touched it. The plants on the iron gate had just been cut, and the large gardens were perfect. A very old caretaker and a few house servants welcomed us. It would be a big job to make the house as modern as the town nearby, but the servants' warm welcome took away our last worries. When we found my family's laboratory, what had been planned as a short visit became a stay without an end.
ParadoxIntro.5.short: The estate seemed untouched by its years of vacancy, the grounds immaculate. An aged caretaker and small staff welcomed us warmly. Modernizing it would be daunting, but once we found the laboratory, our visit became indefinite.

ParadoxIntro.6.full: When I spoke of my family's history of experimentation, I was rarely met with indifference but more often firm words of encouragement. It appeared that this region, so rife with abnormal progress, viewed my theories as rudimentary but delightfully avant-garde. Even when I expounded upon dark rituals and the grotesque, they encouraged further exploration and referred me to the newly constructed University.
ParadoxIntro.6.easy: When I talked about my family's history of experiments, people were rarely uninterested. More often they encouraged me strongly. It seemed that in this region, which was so full of unusual progress, people thought my theories were simple but wonderfully new and daring. Even when I talked about dark rituals and horrible things, they told me to explore further and sent me to the new University.
ParadoxIntro.6.short: My family's experiments drew not indifference but encouragement. This region of strange progress found my theories basic yet delightfully avant-garde, and even my talk of dark rituals earned a referral to the new University.

ParadoxIntro.7.full: This caused me severe consternation. Was this not what I wanted — a clear path towards scientific enlightenment and support of my family's landmark ideas? Why did their lack of friction vex me so? Did they view my illustrious work as trivial?
ParadoxIntro.7.easy: This troubled me very much. Was this not what I wanted, a clear path towards scientific understanding and support for my family's important ideas? Why did it annoy me so much that nobody was against me? Did they think my great work was unimportant?
ParadoxIntro.7.short: This deeply troubled me. Was this not what I wanted? Why did their lack of resistance vex me? Did they think my work trivial?

ParadoxIntro.8.full: It was this grim realization that strengthened my will. If these craven modernists wanted more, then so be it! I would push the limits of science further than ever before and damn the consequences!
ParadoxIntro.8.easy: It was this dark understanding that made my will stronger. If these cowardly modern people wanted more, then they would get it! I would push the limits of science further than ever before, whatever the consequences!
ParadoxIntro.8.short: That grim realization steeled me. If these craven modernists wanted more, so be it! I would push science further than ever, consequences be damned!

TimeTravelIntro2.2.full: If you disbelieve the next portion of my story, I would think you of sound mind to do so. I will withhold the specific details of the location, but the cryptic map led us to an abandoned silver mine near the ruined village. With lanterns held high, my cousins and I crept forward into the darkened mineshaft, following the curve of iron tracks to an alcove where warning signs had been posted by the last workers years ago.
TimeTravelIntro2.2.easy: If you do not believe the next part of my story, I would think you are sensible. I will not tell you exactly where it was, but the mysterious map took us to an old silver mine near the ruined village. With our lamps held high, my cousins and I moved slowly into the dark mine. We followed the curve of the iron tracks to a small space where the last workers had put up warning signs years ago.
TimeTravelIntro2.2.short: You would be wise to doubt what follows. The cryptic map led us to an abandoned silver mine near the ruined village. Lanterns high, my cousins and I followed the rails into the dark, to an alcove posted with old warning signs.

TimeTravelIntro2.3.full: As we approached, a metal box began to hum. Blue sparks crackled from the edges of the box, fully illuminating the cave. With a sudden flash, a door on the metal device swung open and thick fog cascaded along the rails. Coincidentally, {0} leather seats were situated against the interior walls of the machine.
TimeTravelIntro2.3.easy: As we came closer, a metal box began to hum. Blue sparks cracked from the edges of the box, and they lit up the whole cave. With a sudden flash, a door on the metal machine swung open, and thick fog flowed along the tracks. By chance, there were {0} leather seats along the inside walls of the machine.
TimeTravelIntro2.3.short: As we neared, a metal box began to hum, blue sparks lighting the cave. With a flash its door swung open, fog spilling along the rails. Inside, by coincidence, were {0} leather seats.

TimeTravelIntro2.4.full: Without a moment's deliberation, we ambled through the entrance and buckled ourselves in. As we each tightened the buckles about us, we heard a loud hissing sound like the escaping of steam through unseen vents, and the door slammed shut. The metallic walls shook violently, jolting us against our constraints.
TimeTravelIntro2.4.easy: Without thinking for a moment, we walked through the entrance and put on our belts. As each of us tightened the belts, we heard a loud hissing sound, like steam escaping through hidden holes, and the door slammed shut. The metal walls shook violently and threw us against our belts.
TimeTravelIntro2.4.short: Without hesitation we climbed in and buckled up. Steam hissed, the door slammed shut, and the walls shook violently around us.

MonarchReignIntro.2.full: Influence is gained in two ways: through money (that alluring and insidious scratch) and through bloodshed. Though my years on this foul Earth are few, in this abbreviated time I have learned this one valuable truth.
MonarchReignIntro.2.easy: You get influence in two ways: with money (that attractive and dangerous stuff) and with bloodshed. I do not have many years left on this terrible Earth, but in this short time I have learned this one valuable truth.
MonarchReignIntro.2.short: Influence comes two ways: money and bloodshed. In my short time on this foul Earth, I have learned this valuable truth.

MonarchReignIntro.3.full: The voracious objections of the townsfolk had become so commonplace that to see them reduced to sneering murmurs was a marked improvement that made my excursions to the village supremely more tolerable. The Separatist movement had dissipated with time, which put an end to this exasperating (yet lucrative) warring business and the peasantry returned to their normal state of impotent discontent.
MonarchReignIntro.3.easy: The angry complaints of the townspeople had become so normal that it was a big improvement to hear only quiet, unfriendly whispers now, and my trips to the village became much easier. With time, the Separatist movement had disappeared. This ended the annoying (but profitable) business of war, and the farmers went back to being unhappy without any power, as usual.
MonarchReignIntro.3.short: The townsfolk's loud objections had dwindled to sneering murmurs, making my visits far more tolerable. The Separatists had faded, ending the tiresome (but lucrative) war, and the peasants returned to their usual impotent discontent.

MonarchReignIntro.4.full: By this time, our family's influence had bent the ear of the throne. With keen use of investment capital, we were afforded an advisory position that could be employed to sway official opinion and deal with regional matters. This presented a delicate balance: As long as our work went unnoticed, we could avoid all consequences and remain influential. Once noticed, however, we could never return to the same peace once afforded. Heavy is the head that wears the crown, as the bard says.
MonarchReignIntro.4.easy: By this time, our family had enough influence that the king listened to us. By investing our money cleverly, we got a position as advisors, which we could use to change official opinions and handle matters in the region. This was a careful balance: as long as nobody noticed our work, we could avoid all consequences and keep our influence. But once someone noticed, we could never go back to the same peace. As the poet says, the head that wears the crown is heavy.
MonarchReignIntro.4.short: By now our family had the throne's ear. Our investments bought an advisory post to sway opinion and regional matters. A delicate balance: unnoticed, we kept our influence; once noticed, never again our peace. Heavy is the head that wears the crown.

MonarchReignIntro.5.full: I was excited at the proposition, and instructed my servants to be at their finest for potential visitors; because while I grew lethargic at the thought of entertaining clerical matters of the crown, I fully recognized the power that one could wield with proper control of the state. And whether I had to bury them in gold or watch the rivers run red with blood, I would be afforded that power!
MonarchReignIntro.5.easy: I was excited by the offer and told my servants to be at their best for possible visitors. The thought of dealing with the boring paperwork of the crown made me tired, but I fully understood how much power you can have when you control the state well. And whether I had to bury them in gold or watch the rivers turn red with blood, I would get that power!
MonarchReignIntro.5.short: Excited, I told my servants to be ready for visitors. Crown paperwork bores me, but I knew the power that control of the state brings, and whether by gold or by rivers of blood, it would be mine!

PeaceIntro.2.full: I arrived just in time for the festivities. The normally dour gothic architecture was festooned with brightly colored ribbons, balloons, and pots overflowing with borscht. The conquering soldiers paraded down the cobblestone streets in formation and uniform, ticker tape celebrating the Separatists’ victory. Such a remarkable contrast between the slipshod militias of my youth and the democratic revolutionaries cheering the Hungarian name in time with each stomp of a soldier's boot.
PeaceIntro.2.easy: I arrived just in time for the celebrations. The usually dark, gothic buildings were decorated with colorful ribbons, balloons, and pots full of borscht soup. The winning soldiers marched in uniform and in lines down the stone streets, and paper strips flew in the air to celebrate the Separatists' victory. What a big difference between the badly organized fighters of my youth and the democratic revolutionaries who cheered for Hungary with every step of a soldier's boot.
PeaceIntro.2.short: I arrived in time for the festivities: gothic streets decked with ribbons, balloons and pots of borscht, soldiers parading amid ticker tape for the Separatists' victory. How different from the ragged militias of my youth.

PeaceIntro.3.full: However, it was not this boring pageantry that ignited an infernal passion within me, it was the passion of the people. Emboldened by their conquest of a royal power and enlivened with pride in their country, this righteous fervor became a frenzy. Within weeks, an extreme nationalist party began to take hold and this brief respite from war was suddenly punctuated by lofty ambitions.
PeaceIntro.3.easy: But it was not this boring show that lit a burning passion in me. It was the passion of the people. They had won against a royal power and were proud of their country, and their feeling of being right became madness. In a few weeks, an extreme nationalist party began to grow, and this short break from war suddenly ended with big ambitions.
PeaceIntro.3.short: But it was the people's passion, not the pageantry, that fired me. Emboldened by victory over the crown, their pride became a frenzy, and within weeks an extreme nationalist party took hold, with lofty ambitions.

PeaceIntro.4.full: The government had realized that the only way to ensure a lasting peace in the country and the tumultuous surrounding territories was to properly exercise military force to coerce cooperation. My family's reputation within the scientific community had positioned me as the foremost authority in experimental weaponry. I relished the opportunity to observe the devastative effects of these marvelous machinations by attempting to take over the world.
PeaceIntro.4.easy: The government had understood that the only way to make sure there would be a long peace in the country and the troubled lands around it was to use military force to make others cooperate. Because of my family's name among scientists, I was now the most important expert on experimental weapons. I loved the chance to watch the destructive effects of these wonderful machines, by trying to take over the world.
PeaceIntro.4.short: The government decided lasting peace required military force to coerce cooperation. My family's reputation made me the foremost expert in experimental weaponry, and I relished watching my marvelous machines in action as we set out to conquer the world.

PeaceIntro.5.full: With my technological arsenal leading the charge, no nation could hope to resist our power! Our army would ensure a lasting peace that would enshrine my legacy forever in the annals of human history. There was not a moment to waste! It was time to change the world with science!
PeaceIntro.5.easy: With my technological weapons in front, no nation could hope to resist our power! Our army would make sure there was a long peace that would keep my name in human history forever. There was no time to lose! It was time to change the world with science!
PeaceIntro.5.short: With my arsenal leading the charge, no nation could resist! Our army would secure a peace that enshrined my legacy forever. It was time to change the world with science!

PeaceEvent.2.full: My ingenious creations had successfully turned the tide of the World War in our favor. With the entirety of the Eastern European front coalescing to our demands and the remainder of the continent on the verge of surrender, it was clear that no force on the planet was stronger than our nation.
PeaceEvent.2.easy: My clever creations had turned the World War in our favor. The whole Eastern European front was giving in to our demands, and the rest of the continent was close to surrendering. It was clear that no power on the planet was stronger than our nation.
PeaceEvent.2.short: My creations had turned the World War our way. Eastern Europe yielded, the rest of the continent was near surrender; no nation was stronger than ours.

PeaceEvent.3.full: However, the consistent uprisings and insurgent activities among the populace was diverting our precious resources. The generals feared that without loyal public support an insurrection could topple all of our designs from the inside.
PeaceEvent.3.easy: But the constant rebellions and attacks among the people were taking away our valuable resources. The generals were afraid that without loyal support from the people, a rebellion could destroy all our plans from the inside.
PeaceEvent.3.short: But constant uprisings drained our resources, and the generals feared an insurrection could topple everything from within.

PeaceEvent.4.full: It was suggested that we should embark on an aggressive propaganda campaign that promoted our values of freedom and national pride to motivate the people. Alternatively, modern advancements in chemistry were astonishing. It would be a simple matter to make an example of a single city by strategically releasing a mustard gas concoction. An inexpensive and very effective solution.
PeaceEvent.4.easy: Someone suggested that we should start a strong propaganda campaign, to promote our values of freedom and national pride and to motivate the people. On the other hand, modern discoveries in chemistry were amazing. It would be easy to punish a single city as an example, by carefully releasing a mustard gas mixture. A cheap and very effective solution.
PeaceEvent.4.short: One proposal was an aggressive propaganda campaign promoting freedom and national pride. The other: make an example of a single city with mustard gas. Cheap and very effective.

TimeTravelEvent.2.full: While the journal was an astonishing discovery in itself, I did not realize that the true revelation would arrive several weeks later while I sampled brandy upon my veranda. A swirl of stormclouds suddenly converged overhead, and with a spear of electricity a fantastic metal contraption appeared. The {0} travelers emerged, wrinkles lining their features and gray, wispy hair held back by jeweler's goggles strapped to their heads.
TimeTravelEvent.2.easy: The journal was an amazing discovery in itself, but I did not know that the real surprise would come several weeks later, while I was tasting brandy on my veranda. Suddenly, storm clouds came together above me, and with a bolt of lightning, a fantastic metal machine appeared. The {0} travelers came out. Their faces had wrinkles, and their gray, thin hair was held back by jeweler's goggles on their heads.
TimeTravelEvent.2.short: The journal was astonishing, but the true revelation came weeks later. As I sipped brandy on my veranda, stormclouds gathered and, with a spear of lightning, a metal contraption appeared. Out stepped {0} wrinkled travelers, wispy gray hair held back by jeweler's goggles.

TimeTravelEvent.3.full: Our meeting was brief, but over a brunch of polenta and egg-plant stuffed with forcemeat, they relinquished control of several new schematics which they claimed had been retrieved from the future and would revolutionize the modern world. As one may have surmised from this encounter, the intrepid traveler was none other than my long-lost parent, here to entrust one final piece of my legacy.
TimeTravelEvent.3.easy: Our meeting was short, but over a late breakfast of polenta and eggplant filled with meat, they gave me several new plans. They said they had brought these back from the future and that they would change the modern world completely. As you may have guessed, the brave traveler was nobody else than my parent, who had been lost for so long and had come to give me one last piece of my family's work.
TimeTravelEvent.3.short: Over a brief brunch, they handed over schematics retrieved from the future that would revolutionize the world. The traveler was, as you may guess, my long-lost parent, entrusting me with one final piece of my legacy.

TimeTravelEvent.4.full: With these experiments, they implored, I could work towards a true Utopia - a world of technological perfection.
TimeTravelEvent.4.easy: With these experiments, they begged me, I could work towards a real Utopia: a world where technology is perfect.

BlameGameEvent.2.full: But this was inadequate! Was I to gamble the life's work of not one but two generations on a single vote? If this war continued, all that we had created would be lost! How could my cousins not realize the tenuous position thrust upon us? To experiment and perish or to spend my days ignoring that which I most desired; the choice was unbearable!
BlameGameEvent.2.easy: But this was not enough! Should I risk the life's work of not one but two generations on a single vote? If this war continued, everything we had made would be lost! How could my cousins not see the dangerous position we were in? To do experiments and die, or to spend my days ignoring what I wanted most: the choice was unbearable!
BlameGameEvent.2.short: Inadequate! Gamble two generations' work on a single vote? If the war went on, all would be lost! To experiment and perish, or ignore what I most desired; the choice was unbearable!

BlameGameEvent.3.full: I felt that we needed a more decisive solution and I expressed several plans, which were unceremoniously dismissed by my simple-minded cousins.
BlameGameEvent.3.easy: I felt that we needed a stronger solution, and I suggested several plans, but my simple-minded cousins rudely refused them.

BlameGameEvent.4.full: But it was when I was bedridden, at my lowest point, sick with despair, that a knock on my door roused me from my convalescence. Little did I realize that the answer to our quandary would arrive right at my doorstep.
BlameGameEvent.4.easy: But when I was sick in bed, at my lowest point, full of despair, a knock on my door woke me from my recovery. I did not know that the answer to our problem would come right to my door.
BlameGameEvent.4.short: But at my lowest, bedridden with despair, a knock at my door roused me. The answer had arrived on my doorstep.

WarningIntro.3.full: While the discovery of my family's experiments and journals would cement my scientific ambitions for years to come, I had never actually met them. I was too young to remember the disappearance of my brilliant progenitor. To lose a parent and then another to the subsequent dementia that followed was more folly than one child should ever have to bear. I was shielded from this reality, rushed away to Vienna, where I was consumed by my studies until my twenty-first year. It was only at my partner's insistence that I decided to settle my inheritance.
WarningIntro.3.easy: Finding my family's experiments and journals would decide my scientific plans for many years, but I had never really met them. I was too young to remember when my brilliant ancestor disappeared. Losing one parent, and then the other to the madness that followed, was more than one child should ever have to carry. They protected me from this truth and sent me quickly to Vienna, where I was busy with my studies until I was twenty-one. Only because my partner insisted did I decide to take care of my inheritance.
WarningIntro.3.short: My family's journals would shape my ambitions, yet I never knew them. I was too young to remember my brilliant progenitor's disappearance, or the dementia that took my other parent. Sheltered in Vienna until twenty-one, I came to settle my inheritance only at my partner's insistence.

WarningIntro.4.full: I remember being stunned as I arrived by train on a mid-summer's evening. I do not know what I expected from the anecdotes my nanny had relayed to me, but it  was not the bustling cityscape that greeted me. As the sun dipped into the forest, the glimmer of modern steel light fixtures amplified the urban luminescence. My delighted spouse and I enjoyed a quiet ride in our steamer car which offered us a chance to observe the idyllic community and decidedly pleasant folk enjoying the convenience of electricity and steam turbine technology.
WarningIntro.4.easy: I remember how surprised I was when I arrived by train on an evening in the middle of summer. I do not know what I expected from the stories my nanny had told me, but it was not the busy city that welcomed me. As the sun went down behind the forest, the shine of modern steel lamps made the city lights even brighter. My happy spouse and I enjoyed a quiet ride in our steam car, which gave us a chance to see the perfect community and the very friendly people, who enjoyed the comfort of electricity and steam machines.
WarningIntro.4.short: Arriving by train on a midsummer evening, I was stunned: not the village of my nanny's tales, but a bustling, modern town glowing with steel lamps. From our steamer car, my spouse and I admired the pleasant folk enjoying electricity and steam.

WarningIntro.5.full: The estate appeared untouched by years of vacancy; recently pruned brambles and ivy adorned the iron gate and the expansive grounds were immaculate. A caretaker of great age and a small housekeeping staff greeted us. Although updating the grounds to the more modern standard of the nearby town would prove a daunting task, the servants’ warm reception allayed our remaining anxieties. Upon discovery of my family's laboratory, what had been planned as a mere visit received an indefinite extension.
WarningIntro.5.easy: The house looked as if all the years without anyone living in it had not touched it. The plants on the iron gate had just been cut, and the large gardens were perfect. A very old caretaker and a few house servants welcomed us. It would be a big job to make the house as modern as the town nearby, but the servants' warm welcome took away our last worries. When we found my family's laboratory, what had been planned as a short visit became a stay without an end.
WarningIntro.5.short: The estate seemed untouched by its years of vacancy, the grounds immaculate. An aged caretaker and small staff welcomed us warmly. Modernizing it would be daunting, but once we found the laboratory, our visit became indefinite.

WarningIntro.6.full: However, when I spoke of my family's history of experimentation, I was rarely met with indifference but more often firm words of encouragement. It appeared that this region, so rife with abnormal progress, viewed my theories as rudimentary but delightfully avant-garde. Even when I expounded upon dark rituals and the grotesque, they encouraged further exploration and referred me to the newly constructed University.
WarningIntro.6.easy: But when I talked about my family's history of experiments, people were rarely uninterested. More often they encouraged me strongly. It seemed that in this region, which was so full of unusual progress, people thought my theories were simple but wonderfully new and daring. Even when I talked about dark rituals and horrible things, they told me to explore further and sent me to the new University.
WarningIntro.6.short: My family's experiments drew not indifference but encouragement. This region of strange progress found my theories basic yet delightfully avant-garde, and even my talk of dark rituals earned a referral to the new University.

WarningIntro.7.full: This caused me severe consternation. Was this not what I wanted — a clear path towards scientific enlightenment and support of my family's landmark ideas? Why did their lack of friction vex me so? Did they view my illustrious work as trivial?
WarningIntro.7.easy: This troubled me very much. Was this not what I wanted, a clear path towards scientific understanding and support for my family's important ideas? Why did it annoy me so much that nobody was against me? Did they think my great work was unimportant?
WarningIntro.7.short: This deeply troubled me. Was this not what I wanted? Why did their lack of resistance vex me? Did they think my work trivial?

WarningIntro.8.full: It was this grim realization that strengthened my will. If these craven modernists wanted more, then so be it! I would push the limits of science further than ever before and damn the consequences!
WarningIntro.8.easy: It was this dark understanding that made my will stronger. If these cowardly modern people wanted more, then they would get it! I would push the limits of science further than ever before, whatever the consequences!
WarningIntro.8.short: That grim realization steeled me. If these craven modernists wanted more, so be it! I would push science further than ever, consequences be damned!

WarningEvent.12.easy: "I am too late! It is already happening!" she screamed, before the world changed itself around her.

TimeTravelintro1.2.full: I hope you will indulge my brief melancholic digression, for even my stern disposition was reduced to sobbing when I discovered the grim remnants of what was once a burgeoning village. I knew of the tragedy, having received several letters urging me to delay my visit until the conflict had been resolved. However, I felt compelled to see the destruction with my own eyes, and even braved the last vestiges of war to do so. If only I had taken heed of their warning...
TimeTravelintro1.2.easy: I hope you will forgive me for a short, sad story, because even I, with my hard character, cried when I found the dark remains of what was once a growing village. I knew about the tragedy, because I had received several letters asking me to wait with my visit until the conflict was over. But I felt I had to see the destruction with my own eyes, and I even faced the last parts of the war to do it. If only I had listened to their warning...
TimeTravelintro1.2.short: Forgive this melancholy digression: even I sobbed at the grim remains of the once thriving village. Letters had urged me to wait until the conflict ended, but I had to see it with my own eyes. If only I had listened...

TimeTravelintro1.3.full: The all-encompassing destruction had blackened the fields, leaving the land ashen and emaciated. The once-grand estate was now in shambles; a dilapidated husk of its former intimidating presence. I wept for what seemed like hours amongst the dust and rubble. While I was still heir to a considerable fortune with diverse business interests, I was struck by the sentimental weight of such a loss.
TimeTravelintro1.3.easy: The destruction was everywhere. It had made the fields black and left the land gray and dead. The once-great house was now in pieces, an empty, broken shell of the frightening building it once was. I cried for what felt like hours among the dust and stones. I still had a large fortune and many different businesses, but the loss felt very heavy to me.
TimeTravelintro1.3.short: The fields were blackened, the land ashen, the grand estate a ruined husk. I wept for hours in the rubble. Though still heir to a fortune, I felt the loss deeply.

TimeTravelintro1.4.full: However, fortune would soon shine its myriad gaze upon me.
TimeTravelintro1.4.easy: But soon, luck would smile on me in many ways.

TimeTravelintro1.5.full: I was joined by my cousins and we shared our grief at a hotel in Budapest for several days. It was there that an unexpected messenger arrived with a small brown package. Inside, the executor of our parents’ affairs had included the remaining articles of interest salvaged from the mansion. As if preserved for this moment, there was a leather journal seemingly untouched by the flames. Upon opening the tome, a weathered sheet of parchment fell to the table.
TimeTravelintro1.5.easy: My cousins joined me, and we were sad together in a hotel in Budapest for several days. There, a messenger we did not expect arrived with a small brown package. Inside, the person who handled our parents' inheritance had put the last interesting things that were saved from the big house. As if it had been kept for this moment, there was a leather journal that the flames seemed not to have touched. When I opened the book, an old sheet of paper fell onto the table.
TimeTravelintro1.5.short: My cousins and I grieved together in a Budapest hotel. There a messenger brought a package from our parents' executor: items saved from the mansion, including a leather journal untouched by the flames. When I opened it, a weathered page fell out.

MartialSepEvent.2.full: As the war pressed on relentlessly, it was I who suffered most terribly. With embattlements requiring constant provisions, procuring the necessary ingredients for my experiments became increasingly more difficult.
MartialSepEvent.2.easy: As the war went on without stopping, it was I who suffered the most. The soldiers at the front always needed supplies, so it became harder and harder to get the ingredients I needed for my experiments.

MartialSepEvent.3.full: However, in my humble brilliance I settled on a firm solution based upon one simple question: Why do I need specialty ingredients when I can just attach guns to everything?
MartialSepEvent.3.easy: But with my modest genius, I found a clear solution based on one simple question: Why do I need special ingredients when I can just put guns on everything?

MartialSepEvent.4.full: Certainly this slapdash methodology was not ideal nor dignified, but it certainly achieved a devastative result. Why my first practical demonstration caused both sides to cease hostilities after witnessing a small battalion reduced to a mere wine stain upon the battlefield.
MartialSepEvent.4.easy: This careless method was certainly not perfect or dignified, but it certainly destroyed a lot. My first practical demonstration even made both sides stop fighting, after they saw a small group of soldiers turned into nothing more than a wine stain on the battlefield.
MartialSepEvent.4.short: Crude and undignified, perhaps, but devastating: my first demonstration reduced a small battalion to a wine stain, and both sides ceased hostilities.

MartialSepEvent.5.full: However, the regional military factions required additional convincing as the use of our weapons was still considered a "war crime" and would require further convincing to employ these additional methods. Imagine, "science" being considered a war crime? Is it not a general's hope to reach an efficient victory?
MartialSepEvent.5.easy: But the military groups in the region needed more convincing, because using our weapons was still called a "war crime", and more convincing was needed before they would use these extra methods. Can you imagine, "science" called a war crime? Does a general not hope to win efficiently?
MartialSepEvent.5.short: But the regional military still called our weapons a "war crime" and needed more convincing. Science, a war crime? Does a general not want an efficient victory?

BlameOut1.2.full: In an attempt to pacify the local military, my cousins and I mutually agreed to assign blame for their enemies' intelligence onto one of our own.
BlameOut1.2.easy: To calm the local military, my cousins and I agreed together to blame one of us for giving information to their enemies.

BlameOut1.3.full: **{0}** arrived home from a weekend sojourn to discover that their Estate had been ransacked by the soldiers. In a barbaric display against disloyalty, a portion of the domain had been set ablaze. Fortunately, the caretaker and servants were able to stave off the fire before it consumed the entirety of the lot.
BlameOut1.3.easy: **{0}** came home from a weekend trip and found that the soldiers had searched and damaged their house. To punish disloyalty in a cruel way, they had set fire to part of the property. Luckily, the caretaker and the servants were able to stop the fire before it burned everything.
BlameOut1.3.short: **{0}** returned from a weekend away to find their Estate ransacked by soldiers and partly set ablaze. Luckily, the staff stopped the fire before it consumed everything.

They were notably displeased with our bickering and the wasted time they invested into inquiries around the villa.
BlameOut2.2.easy: Several of us pointed at each other in a show of small competition, and the soldiers could not find a traitor **with more votes than the others** among us. They were clearly unhappy about our arguing and the time they had wasted asking questions around the house.
BlameOut2.2.short: We pointed fingers at each other, and the soldiers could find no traitor **with more votes than the others**. They were displeased with our bickering and their wasted time.

BlameOut2.3.full: In a blunt exertion of power, the soldiers excised a tax from myself and all of my cousins, which we were obliged to pay under threat of bodily injury. I pledged my distinguished service in scientific pursuits to their cause, which they vehemently (and rudely) declined.
BlameOut2.3.easy: To show their power directly, the soldiers took a tax from me and from all my cousins, which we had to pay or be hurt. I offered my excellent service in science to their cause, but they refused strongly (and rudely).
BlameOut2.3.short: In a blunt show of power, the soldiers taxed all of us under threat of injury. They rudely declined my offer of scientific service.

RumorCreep.2.easy: The townspeople noticed how curious I was, and it seemed that my conversation with the homeless man had caused excitement among the local gossips. I decided to keep my meetings more secret in the future.

RumorIngredient.2.full: A local farmer had observed my conversation, and after determining an agreeable moment to greet me, we engaged in a cordial chat about the local economy. The earthy individual even suggested a visit to his plantation, which turned out to be most advantageous.
RumorIngredient.2.easy: A local farmer had seen my conversation. He waited for a good moment to greet me, and then we had a friendly talk about the local economy. This simple man even suggested a visit to his farm, which turned out to be very useful.

RumorKnowledge.2.full: While it seemed anomalous to me at the time, when my conversation ended I was immediately greeted by a fellow who introduced himself as one who shared an affinity for the scientific. I was intrigued and invited the young man in the brown sack suit to dine with me at a local cafe. Admittedly, my university knowledge was the main course, but I was still able to glean a few novel tidbits.
RumorKnowledge.2.easy: It seemed strange to me at the time, but when my conversation ended, a man greeted me at once and said that he also loved science. I was interested and invited the young man in the brown suit to eat with me at a local cafe. I must admit that my university knowledge was the main course, but I was still able to learn a few new little things.
RumorKnowledge.2.short: Afterwards, a young man in a brown suit introduced himself as a fellow lover of science. Over lunch, my university knowledge was the main course, but I still gleaned a few novel tidbits.

So when our conversation concluded, I spent the next few hours introducing myself to the less than charming group of locals that frequently attended political meetings. While they may not have fully comprehended the intelligence I exuded, there was certainly an air of cheerfulness when I exited the building.
RumorPitch.2.easy: At university, I was always very good at speaking in public. So when our conversation ended, I spent the next few hours introducing myself to the not very charming group of local people who often came to political meetings. They may not have fully understood how intelligent I am, but there was certainly a happy feeling when I left the building.
RumorPitch.2.short: Ever a skilled public speaker, I spent hours charming the regulars at the political meetings. They may not have grasped my intelligence, but spirits were high when I left.

CostStick.2.full: I could not determine why I had held onto such a grotesque, amateurish item. However, although I had no scientific basis for the assessment, it's presence appeared to provide an aura of good fortune. My endeavors were more easily bolstered and my resolution firmer upon viewing it.
CostStick.2.easy: I could not understand why I had kept such an ugly, badly made thing. But even though I had no scientific reason to think so, it seemed to bring good luck. When I looked at it, my work was easier to support and my will was stronger.
CostStick.2.short: Why I kept such a grotesque, amateurish thing I cannot say, yet it seemed to bring good fortune. My work prospered and my resolve grew firmer.

ResistEnd2.2.easy: Modern weapons may change the result of a battle, but if the army has no money to build these weapons and give them to their soldiers, they will lose the war in the end. It was this promise of loyalty that finally decided the result of the war.
ResistEnd2.2.short: Advanced weapons may turn a battle, but without money to build and supply them, a war is lost. It was this pledge of allegiance that decided the outcome.

TTIntro3.2.full: As quickly as it had begun, the peculiar room fell silent. The door of the chamber fell from its hinges, flat to the earth, sparks and smoke billowing from the opening.
TTIntro3.2.easy: As quickly as it had started, the strange room became silent. The door of the room fell off its hinges, flat onto the ground, and sparks and smoke came out of the opening.

TTIntro3.3.full: We emerged from the mineshaft and made haste to the village. The changes were immediately obvious: The town had been returned to its former state, as it was in 1831. We knew that providence and some unseen benefactor had given us an opportunity to change the mistakes of the past and recreate a brighter future.
TTIntro3.3.easy: We came out of the mine and hurried to the village. We saw the changes at once: the town was back as it used to be, as it was in 1831. We knew that fate and some unseen helper had given us a chance to fix the mistakes of the past and make a brighter future.
TTIntro3.3.short: We hurried from the mine to the village. It was 1831 again. Providence had given us a chance to undo the past and build a brighter future.

TTIntro3.4.full: I rushed to my Estate to be greeted by a familiar sight from my youth; the gothic iron and stone as formidable as I remembered. With a well-crafted farce, I introduced myself to my youthful parents as a relative on holiday. I quickly ingratiated myself into the fold and resolved to continue my experiments, searching for a way to return to my time, while also ensuring that history would not repeat itself.
TTIntro3.4.easy: I hurried to my house and was greeted by a familiar sight from my youth: the dark iron and stone, as frightening as I remembered. With a clever act, I introduced myself to my young parents as a relative on holiday. I quickly became part of the family and decided to continue my experiments. I looked for a way to go back to my own time, while also making sure that history would not repeat itself.
TTIntro3.4.short: At my Estate, the gothic iron and stone were as formidable as I remembered. Posing as a relative on holiday, I won over my young parents and continued my experiments, seeking a way home while making sure history would not repeat itself.

TTIntro3.5.full: Time, it appeared, was not on my side.
TTIntro3.5.easy: It seemed that time was not on my side.

ParadoxFirst.2.full: When I discovered the journal, the masterwork plans, and the clandestine fragments of experiments in the laboratory, I laughed. Surely, my great-grandfather had grandiose ambitions at the time, but modern advancements made many of the blueprints obsolete and frankly, a bit cute.
ParadoxFirst.2.easy: When I found the journal, the masterwork plans, and the secret pieces of experiments in the laboratory, I laughed. My great-grandfather surely had big ambitions at the time, but modern progress had made many of the plans old-fashioned and, to be honest, a little cute.
ParadoxFirst.2.short: When I found the journal, plans and secret experiments, I laughed. My great-grandfather's ambitions were grand, but modern advances made many blueprints obsolete, and frankly, a bit cute.

ParadoxFirst.3.full: I decided to improve upon them, and I knew just the thing that would dazzle them all!
ParadoxFirst.3.easy: I decided to make them better, and I knew exactly what would amaze them all!

I realized that, if the important experiments of the previous generation remained incomplete, the consequences were unknown and potentially catastrophic.
TimeTokens.2.easy: They had been destroyed (or had completely rotted) before I could see them being made, but I knew that my presence could change the natural order of things. I understood that if the important experiments of the last generation stayed unfinished, nobody knew what would happen, and it could be a disaster.
TimeTokens.2.short: They were destroyed before I could see them made, but I knew my presence could alter the natural order. If the previous generation's important experiments stayed incomplete, the consequences could be catastrophic.

TimeTokens.3.full: Oh the chaotic potential this offered! I could not resist grinning.
TimeTokens.3.easy: Oh, the chaos that this could bring! I could not stop smiling.

PeaceEventGas.2.full: The ends justify the means. Through conquest of the world, we could finally enforce peace by removing the ills of humanity. The people would soon understand that without complete submission there would never be an end to conflict. With a few strategically placed charges, the gas filtered through the city. The massacre left thousands dead and countless citizens scarred permanently through the inhalation of the deadly chemical solution.
PeaceEventGas.2.easy: The goal makes the method right. By taking over the world, we could finally force peace by removing the illnesses of humanity. The people would soon understand that without complete obedience, conflict would never end. With a few well-placed bombs, the gas spread through the city. The massacre left thousands of people dead and many others hurt forever because they breathed in the deadly chemicals.
PeaceEventGas.2.short: The ends justify the means. Only by conquering the world could we enforce peace. A few well-placed charges spread the gas through the city, leaving thousands dead and countless more scarred.

PeaceEventGas.3.full: In response to the clinical effectiveness of our actions, the government created a new department of **Public Relations** and asked for one of us to head the department.
PeaceEventGas.3.easy: Because our actions worked so well, the government created a new department of **Public Relations** and asked one of us to lead the department.

PeaceEventGas.4.full: All players **gain 1 {icon:Creepy_Icon}**, **1 {icon:Insanity_Icon}**, and **an Ingredient of their choice.**

PeaceEventNo.2.full: While the confirmation of our own ethical standards both comforted and alarmed us, the military was forced to dispatch additional units to contain the uprising. This distraction was sufficient to significantly slow the advancement of troops across the continent as several minor uprisings were triggered and quashed in newly acquired territories.
PeaceEventNo.2.easy: It was both comforting and worrying for us to see that we still had our own ideas of right and wrong. But the military had to send more soldiers to stop the rebellion. CoWEvent.3.full: The decision could not rest with me alone, unfortunately. But if my cousins - whom I love so dearly - and I, could combine our interests, the aristocracy would surely take note. Would the region be ruled by a monarchy with a strong, **iron fist**, crushing opposition and caring little for the welfare of its citizenry? Or would the **benevolent** rallying of the people serve us best in the end, despite the additional royal scrutiny it would incur?
CoWEvent.3.easy: Sadly, I could not make the decision alone. But if my cousins, whom I love so much, and I could put our interests together, the nobles would surely notice. Would the region be ruled by a monarchy with a strong **iron fist**, which crushes anyone against it and cares little about how its citizens live? Or would a **kind** coming together of the people be best for us in the end, even if it brought more attention from the king?
CoWEvent.3.short: The decision was not mine alone, but if my cousins and I joined forces, the aristocracy would take note. Should the region be ruled with an **iron fist**, crushing all opposition? Or would a **benevolent** rallying of the people serve us better, despite closer royal scrutiny?

CoWEvent.4.full: Perhaps our early actions had already helped confirm our convictions, either way, the time had come to make a decision. For {0}, we knew what was best.
CoWEvent.4.easy: Maybe our early actions had already helped us be sure of what we believed. In any case, the time had come to decide. For {0}, we knew what was best.

TriggerParadox.2.full: The feeling was unlike any I had experienced previously. It was as if I was unknowingly swaddled by the air itself and a cosmic force tore the fabric at the seams, allowing me to burst free. I could feel the timestream mending like the tingle of blood returning to a strangled capillary.
TriggerParadox.2.easy: The feeling was not like anything I had felt before. It was as if the air itself had been wrapped around me without my knowing, and a force from the universe tore the cloth open, so that I could break free. I could feel the stream of time healing, like the tingling when blood comes back into a squeezed vein.
TriggerParadox.2.short: It was as if the air had swaddled me unawares, until a cosmic force tore it open and I burst free. I felt the timestream mend like blood tingling back into a strangled vein.

TriggerParadox.3.full: Unfettered by the pressures of the mundane and reinvigorated by knowledge of the universe's complex inner workings, I surged forward anew!
TriggerParadox.3.easy: Free from the pressure of everyday things, and full of new energy from knowing how the universe works inside, I moved forward again!

TriggerParadox.4.full: Gain **{0}VP** and a Knowledge cube of your choice.

ForewordScen2.1.full: **A Time of War : A Memoir Across Three Generations**

ForewordScen2.2.full: Dear reader, it is with great excitement that I offer this expansive work for your consideration: A recently unearthed, voluminous manuscript – an epic memoir written over the course of three generations. It is a work as monumental and daunting as it is groundbreaking; a glimpse into the inner workings of the true scientific mind.
ForewordScen2.2.easy: Dear reader, I am very excited to offer you this large work to consider: a long handwritten book that was found recently, a great memoir written over three generations. It is a work as huge and difficult as it is new and important: a look inside the real scientific mind.
ForewordScen2.2.short: Dear reader, I am delighted to present a newly unearthed manuscript: an epic memoir spanning three generations, as daunting as it is groundbreaking, and a glimpse into the true scientific mind.

ForewordScen2.3.full: Upon discovery of these immaculate pages, I, suffering great personal expense, set forth to ensure the general publication and distribution of this important history. It is a work that will perhaps elucidate upon and justify the eccentric reputations of my forebears.
ForewordScen2.3.easy: When I found these perfect pages, I paid a lot of my own money to make sure that this important history is published and shared. Maybe it will explain, and even justify, the strange reputations of my ancestors.
ForewordScen2.3.short: At great personal expense, I have seen this important history published. It may explain, and justify, my ancestors' eccentric reputations.

ForewordScen2.4.full: While I admit that I am biased in this appraisal, as it is my own exemplary lineage which is documented, I submit this comprehensive prosopography in as accurate a condition as I can muster. As one will soon attest, it is a chronicle of events of a decidedly fantastical nature, yet my research confirms it to be as true and vital a work as has ever been seen in print.
ForewordScen2.4.easy: I admit that I am not neutral in my opinion, because it is my own excellent family that is described here. But I give you this complete family history in as exact a condition as I can. As you will soon see, it tells of events that are very fantastic, but my research shows that it is as true and as important as any work that has ever been printed.
ForewordScen2.4.short: I admit my bias, as this is my own exemplary lineage, but I present it as accurately as I can. Fantastical as its events are, my research confirms it as true and vital as any work in print.

ForewordScen2.5.full: However, I must offer a word of caution to those with weaker constitutions. While these pages hold a brilliant catalogue of achievements, they also boldly depict the setbacks encountered along the journey. Gruesome, grim, and horrifying as they may be, I have included their spine-chilling contents as originally written. As one might expect, in exposing the base components of the universe, we uncover both light and darkness in equal measure. For without darkness, we cannot appreciate the brilliance of the light.
ForewordScen2.5.easy: But I must warn people who are easily upset. These pages show a brilliant list of successes, but they also show the problems along the way, without hiding them. They may be horrible, dark, and frightening, but I have included their scary contents as they were first written. As you might expect, when we look at the basic parts of the universe, we find light and darkness in equal amounts. Because without darkness, we cannot value how bright the light is.
ForewordScen2.5.short: A warning to the faint of heart: alongside brilliant achievements, these pages show the setbacks too, gruesome as they are, and I have kept them as written. In exposing the universe, we find light and darkness alike; without darkness, we cannot appreciate the light.

RumorD6Guns.1.full: **Carefully pick up this Storybook device and do not allow any other players to see the screen.**

RumorD6Guns.2.full: I distinctly remember the overwhelming stench of lilacs and whatever horrid perfume was in vogue at the time. She was startled as I approached and almost upset the small stack of papers, their faces scrawled with calligraphic writing.
RumorD6Guns.2.easy: I clearly remember the strong smell of lilacs and some terrible perfume that was fashionable at that time. She was surprised when I came closer and almost knocked over the small pile of papers, which were covered in beautiful handwriting.

RumorD6Guns.3.full: "Perhaps, yes," she seemed to perk up at my presence and introduced herself as the mayor's assistant. "Perhaps you could assist me. The village has an important choice to make and yet none have made it."
RumorD6Guns.3.easy: "Maybe, yes," she said, and she seemed to become more lively when she saw me. She said she was the mayor's assistant. "Maybe you could help me. The village has an important choice to make, but nobody has made it yet."

RumorD6Guns.4.full: She offered me a choice which bore more significance than I would have expected. The town wanted to emphasize a unique facet of the local economy that would make the region more alluring to investors.
