RumorD6Confirm.2.full: The woman was visibly relieved by the decision being out of her hands. She would prepare the necessary materials and an announcement would be made.
RumorD6Confirm.2.easy: The woman was clearly relieved that she did not have to decide. She would prepare everything that was needed, and the news would be announced.

RumorD6Confirm.3.full: There was nothing more bountiful than the **knowledge** my family could provide. Whether we would be so generous as to offer our surplus to the village remained to be seen.
RumorD6Confirm.3.easy: Nothing was richer than the **knowledge** my family could give. We would see if we would be generous enough to give what we had extra to the village.

RumorD6Confirm.4.full: From the azalea blossoms to the diversity of species found at the market to the intricate machinery, **goods** were plentiful in the region. It could be very possible that our surplus would be the village's boon.
RumorD6Confirm.4.easy: From the azalea flowers to the many different kinds of animals and plants at the market to the complicated machines, there were many **goods** in the region. It was quite possible that what we had extra would be good for the village.

RumorD6Confirm.5.full: Nothing could be more direct as an alluring investment than **money**. My family would not readily part with it without struggle, but to display it proudly as an advertisement for the locals was certainly an agreeable proposition.
RumorD6Confirm.5.easy: Nothing could be a more direct and attractive investment than **money**. My family would not give it away easily without a fight, but to show it proudly as an advertisement for the locals was certainly a pleasant idea.

IntroConflict.2.full: The spectre of war haunted the small village. This ideological tension would erupt in loud displays and gatherings of the peasantry near the Town Hall. For all the folderol, I began to cherish the moments when the eerie stillness of the evening was broken by anguished yells.
IntroConflict.2.easy: The ghost of war was over the small village. This tension between ideas broke out in loud shows and meetings of the farmers near the Town Hall. In spite of all the noise, I started to love the moments when the strange silence of the evening was broken by painful screams.
IntroConflict.2.short: The spectre of war haunted the village, its tensions erupting in loud gatherings near the Town Hall. Amid the folderol, I came to cherish the evening stillness broken by anguished yells.

IntroConflict.3.full: The Separatists felt alienated by the aristocratic government and wished to secede. Their brash tactics aimed to incite a democratic revolt among the proletariat. The Unified Monarchists feared the anarchic destabilization of the economy at such a key moment during industrialization. I was quickly able to determine that **the town supported the {0}**.
IntroConflict.3.easy: The Separatists felt that the noble government did not care about them, and they wanted to leave the country. Their bold methods tried to start a democratic rebellion among the workers. The Unified Monarchists were afraid that chaos would make the economy unstable at such an important moment of industrial growth. I quickly understood that **the town supported the {0}**.
IntroConflict.3.short: The Separatists, alienated by the aristocratic government, wanted to secede and stirred the workers to revolt. The Unified Monarchists feared economic chaos mid-industrialization. I soon learned that **the town supported the {0}**.

IntroConflict.4.full: Place the {0} Flag card face-up near the Village Chronicle.

ParadoxTimeRandom.2.full: The time device proved to be invaluable for productivity. While the general populace squabbled over self-interests, creating and destroying the countryside in equal measure with varying degrees of incalculable existential horror, I was generally left to my leisure in solitude with my spouse and servants.
ParadoxTimeRandom.2.easy: The time machine was very useful for getting work done. While the people argued about their own interests, and built and destroyed the countryside again and again, with existential horror that you cannot measure, I was mostly left alone in peace with my spouse and servants.
ParadoxTimeRandom.2.short: The time device was invaluable. While the populace squabbled, building and razing the countryside amid incalculable existential horror, I was left in peace with my spouse and servants.

ParadoxTimeRandom.3.full: One flick of an electrical switch and the copper fixtures of the device sent me back to the moments before a failed experiment. I soon became acquainted with visitations from myself, even sharing tea with several versions of my person to talk over and revise a particularly difficult thesis. While the process aged me quicker than desired, the ingredients it saved and the excellent conversation proved well worth it.
ParadoxTimeRandom.3.easy: With one flick of an electric switch, the copper parts of the machine sent me back to the moments before an experiment failed. Soon I got used to visits from myself, and I even had tea with several versions of me to discuss and improve a very difficult theory. The process made me older faster than I wanted, but the ingredients it saved and the excellent conversation were worth it.
ParadoxTimeRandom.3.short: One flick of a switch sent me back to the moments before a failed experiment. I grew used to visits from myself, even sharing tea with several of me over a difficult thesis. It aged me faster than I liked, but the saved ingredients and fine conversation were worth it.

ParadoxTimeRandom.5.full: Technological advancement retrieved from the future, the stability offered by knowing you can change your past, the ability to travel backwards in time to guide one's self away from a rough day ahead; general access to a time machine could lift a near Utopia right to the edge of perfection!
ParadoxTimeRandom.5.easy: Technology brought back from the future, the safety of knowing you can change your past, the ability to travel back in time to help yourself avoid a bad day: if everyone could use a time machine, an almost perfect world could become truly perfect!
ParadoxTimeRandom.5.short: Future technology, a changeable past, the chance to warn yourself of a bad day: time machines for all could lift a near Utopia to perfection!

ParadoxTimeRandom.6.full: While I was somewhat disappointed in the lack of chaos, I was ecstatic at the reaction of the university elite. Our decision had such a positive effect on the world, it made the academics positively seethe! Those furrowed brows and anxious worry lines grafted onto their imbecilic faces made the outcome of this rash decision a joy to behold. It wasn't long before this joy gave way to clarity of purpose. I felt reinvigorated, hoping each day that my next experiment would evoke the same horrific response.
ParadoxTimeRandom.6.easy: I was a little disappointed that there was so little chaos, but I was very happy about the reaction of the important university people. Our decision had such a good effect on the world that it made the scientists really angry! Their worried faces with deep lines on their stupid foreheads made the result of this hasty decision a joy to see. Soon this joy turned into a clear purpose. I felt full of new energy, and every day I hoped that my next experiment would cause the same horrible reaction.
ParadoxTimeRandom.6.short: The lack of chaos disappointed me, but the academics' reaction thrilled me: our decision did so much good it made them seethe! Their furrowed brows were a joy, and soon a purpose. I hoped each new experiment would provoke the same horror.

ParadoxTimeRandom.8.full: If I were to forgo humility for a moment and describe one of my most favorable traits, I am a creature of infinite patience. So, I watched as the first experiments in time alteration bore miniscule results and continued in my tasks without paying them much heed. Like all initial fascinations, the wave of interest in manipulating fate slowly gave way to other technological distractions and time machines became popular children's toys around the holidays.
ParadoxTimeRandom.8.easy: If I may stop being modest for a moment and describe one of my best qualities: I am a creature with endless patience. So I watched as the first experiments in changing time had very small results, and I continued my work without paying much attention to them. Like all new fascinations, the interest in changing fate slowly made room for other technological distractions, and time machines became popular toys for children at holiday time.
ParadoxTimeRandom.8.short: If I may boast: I am infinitely patient. The first experiments in time alteration achieved little, and I paid them no heed. Like all fads, interest faded, and time machines became popular holiday toys for children.

ParadoxTimeRandom.9.full: I cannot recollect the moment when I noticed it, perhaps it happened naturally, but as the timeline shifted ever so slowly, it appeared that the forces aligning the cosmos preferred stasis over the whims of chaos. With each passing season, the studious gap between myself and my cousins seemed to edge ever closer.
ParadoxTimeRandom.9.easy: I cannot remember the moment when I noticed it. Maybe it happened naturally. But as the timeline changed very slowly, it seemed that the forces that order the universe preferred things to stay the same, not the moods of chaos. With every season, the difference in learning between me and my cousins seemed to become smaller.
ParadoxTimeRandom.9.short: I cannot say when I noticed it, but as the timeline slowly shifted, the cosmos seemed to prefer stasis over chaos. Each season, the gap between my cousins and me narrowed.

ParadoxTimeRandom.10.full: And though I abhorred the thought of intervention from forces outside of my understanding, I cannot say that I did not relish my stoicism being rewarded.
ParadoxTimeRandom.10.easy: I hated the thought that forces I did not understand were interfering, but I cannot say that I did not enjoy being rewarded for my calm patience.

ParadoxTimeRandom.12.full: There are narrative consequences for unleashing a Time Machine into the wild, and the devastation is too far-reaching for one single paragraph in a mad scientist's memoir to detail. However, it has **no effect on gameplay** and therefore will be omitted.
ParadoxTimeRandom.12.easy: There are consequences for the story when a Time Machine is let loose in the world, and the destruction is too big to describe in one paragraph in a mad scientist's memoir. But it has **no effect on gameplay**, so it will be left out.

ParadoxTimeRandom.13.full: It is better to write these words now in anticipation of the game, My Father's Work, which will see release in 2022 and detail the historical events of my family. I've played it a few times during my travels and while I wish it had a solo version, it's still very good.
ParadoxTimeRandom.13.easy: It is better to write these words now, before the game My Father's Work comes out in 2022 and tells the historical events of my family. I have played it a few times on my travels, and even though I wish it had a version for one player, it is still very good.

ParadoxTimeRandom.14.full: Perhaps history will no longer align with the narrative presented in the game and this paragraph will seem oddly out of place. Ah, such is the confounding nature of time travel.
ParadoxTimeRandom.14.easy: Maybe history will no longer match the story told in the game, and this paragraph will seem strangely out of place. Ah, time travel is so confusing.

ParadoxTimeRandom.16.full: The people have developed a sense of trust and acceptance for my work after the unmitigated success of the time altering apparatus. Trust and acceptance? I grapple with this concept with many of my waking hours. Even on the days where I feel emboldened to venture backwards into the timestream to undo this stomach-turning adoration, some peon in the village simply undoes my work.
ParadoxTimeRandom.16.easy: After the complete success of the machine that changes time, the people have started to trust and accept my work. Trust and acceptance? I think about this idea for many hours every day. Even on the days when I feel brave enough to go back into the stream of time to undo this love that makes me sick, some unimportant person in the village simply undoes my work.
ParadoxTimeRandom.16.short: After the time apparatus's success, the people trust and accept my work. Trust and acceptance! Even when I travel back to undo this nauseating adoration, some village peon undoes my efforts.

ParadoxTimeRandom.17.full: My beautifully macabre estate is now looked upon with exuberance by tourists to the region. Tourists! By god, this will make pushing the boundaries of ethical imagination nearly impossible! I must break through this irrational barrier of love and generosity before it stifles my work!
ParadoxTimeRandom.17.easy: Tourists who visit the region now look at my beautifully dark house with excitement. Tourists! By god, this will make it almost impossible to push the limits of what is right and wrong! I must break through this senseless wall of love and generosity before it stops my work!
ParadoxTimeRandom.17.short: Tourists now admire my beautifully macabre estate. Tourists! This will make ethical boundary-pushing nearly impossible! I must break this wall of love before it stifles my work!

ParadoxTimeRandom.19.full: How could they accuse us of sedition? The Time Machine was my family's gift to all of humanity and yet they call it willfully negligent and unethical!
ParadoxTimeRandom.19.easy: How could they accuse us of acting against the state? The Time Machine was my family's gift to all humanity, and still they say it is careless on purpose and wrong!

ParadoxTimeRandom.20.full: Do we blame Prometheus for every home burnt to the ground because of the invention of fire? Is the zoetrope responsible for every detestable piece of film created after it? Should we ban perfumes and colognes for their ability to more fervently entice couples into intimacy? It is only natural that the most important discoveries carry with them a modicum of insidious potential.
ParadoxTimeRandom.20.easy: Do we blame Prometheus for every house that burned down because fire was invented? Is the zoetrope responsible for every terrible film made after it? Should we forbid perfumes because they help couples feel closer? It is only natural that the most important discoveries also bring a little dangerous potential.
ParadoxTimeRandom.20.short: Do we blame Prometheus for every house fire? The zoetrope for every terrible film? The greatest discoveries naturally carry some insidious potential.

ParadoxTimeRandom.21.full: It is absurd that a correlative effect is so readily pinned upon me. Yet, their superstitions have once again returned!
ParadoxTimeRandom.21.easy: It is silly that they blame me so easily for something that only happened at the same time. But their superstitions have come back again!

ParadoxTimeRandom.23.full: They discovered who did it. Hungarian government tracked it.
ParadoxTimeRandom.23.easy: They found out who did it. The Hungarian government followed it back.

ParadoxTimeRandom.24.full: Perhaps it was easy to discern this information as every pamphlet, editorial, journal, and detailed blueprint was signed in bold ink. It was all for naught as well. The Hungarian government quietly tracked each copy down with the assistance of the scientific community, and secured this knowledge for themselves alone.
ParadoxTimeRandom.24.easy: Maybe it was easy to find this out, because every leaflet, article, journal, and detailed plan was signed in thick ink. And it was all for nothing. With the help of the scientists, the Hungarian government quietly found every copy and kept this knowledge only for itself.
ParadoxTimeRandom.24.short: Easily done, as everything was signed in bold ink. And all for naught: the government, aided by scientists, quietly tracked down every copy and kept the knowledge for itself.

ParadoxTimeRandom.25.full: My family's decision to disseminate this information had dire consequences for those that chose this path. Their Masterwork was rendered pointless to complete as it would be confiscated immediately by police force emboldened by access to the time stream. Fortunately, those that decided to remain silent could not be implicated merely by association and remained free to continue their work.

ParadoxTimeRandom.27.full: There is always a cycle of destruction and renewal with every major epoch in the world's history, and this would probably be seen as a minor stumbling block in the overall chronology of events. With the ease of general access to a device that had the power to bend time and space around it, it was soon discovered that the average individual may have lacked the self-control and intelligence required to prevent the catastrophic destruction of nearly every living thing in Eastern Europe.
ParadoxTimeRandom.27.easy: In every great period of the world's history, there is always a cycle of destruction and new beginnings, and this would probably be seen as a small problem in the whole history of events. When everyone could easily use a machine that had the power to bend time and space around it, people soon found out that the average person may not have the self-control and intelligence needed to stop the terrible destruction of almost every living thing in Eastern Europe.
ParadoxTimeRandom.27.short: Every epoch has its cycle of destruction and renewal, and this was perhaps a minor stumble. But with a time-bending device in everyone's hands, it turned out the average person lacked the self-control to avoid destroying nearly all life in Eastern Europe.

ParadoxTimeRandom.28.full: Owning an Estate made of stone, looming high above the valley, I was able to retain most of my possessions. Although the air was now tinged with a hint of sulfur and resources were a touch harder to procure.
ParadoxTimeRandom.28.easy: Because I owned a house made of stone, high above the valley, I was able to keep most of my things. But now the air smelled a little of sulfur, and resources were a bit harder to get.

IntroMartial-Monarchists.2.full: If one can call the prospect of perpetual conflict stabilizing, my life settled into a somewhat steady routine. During the day, the sound of distant gunfire rumbled through the halls of my estate as silver plumes of smoke billowed beyond the mountainous horizon, casting tendril-like shadows across the land — a constant reminder of civil war. At night, the rare spectacle of an explosion brightening the sky surprised me with how viscerally I reacted.
IntroMartial-Monarchists.2.easy: If you can call the idea of a war that never ends stable, then my life became quite regular. During the day, the sound of guns far away moved through the halls of my house, while silver clouds of smoke rose behind the mountains and threw long, thin shadows across the land, always reminding us of the civil war. At night, I was surprised by how strongly I reacted to the rare sight of an explosion that lit up the sky.
IntroMartial-Monarchists.2.short: If endless war can be called stable, my life settled into a routine. By day, distant gunfire and smoke over the mountains; by night, the rare explosion lighting the sky, which moved me more than I expected.

IntroMartial-Monarchists.3.full: Soldiers in their bright regalia keep watch over the town from a newly erected outpost, waving the brilliant orange flag of royalty. The Monarchy had claimed victory from afar after stationing their ranks across the region, but as scuffles remained constant, this declaration was all pomp without substance. The Monarchy drafted citizens into their ranks and levied penalties against those who showed disloyalty.
IntroMartial-Monarchists.3.easy: Soldiers in their bright uniforms watch over the town from a new outpost, waving the bright orange flag of the royal family. The Monarchy had said they won, from far away, after placing soldiers all across the region. But the small fights did not stop, so this statement was all show and nothing real. The Monarchy made citizens join the army and punished those who were not loyal.
IntroMartial-Monarchists.3.short: Soldiers in bright regalia watch the town from a new outpost under the royal orange flag. The Monarchy has declared victory, but with skirmishes ongoing it is all pomp. It conscripts citizens and penalizes disloyalty.

IntroMartial-Monarchists.4.full: The inference that one of my standing should owe a debt of servitude to those who already tax my earnings into oblivion was enough to make me spill my tea. And to what end, I wondered? Could peace be mustered in a populace kept so distant from the individuals who ruled it? It was called the industrial revolution for a reason, was it not?
IntroMartial-Monarchists.4.easy: The idea that someone of my position should owe service to the people who already take almost all of my money in taxes made me spill my tea. And for what, I asked myself? Could there be peace among people who are kept so far from the people who rule them? There was a reason it was called the industrial revolution, wasn't there?
IntroMartial-Monarchists.4.short: The notion that one of my standing owed service to those who already tax me into oblivion made me spill my tea. Can there be peace when rulers are so remote? It is called the industrial revolution for a reason.

IntroMartial-Monarchists.5.full: But, I must admit, the safety that the Monarchy afforded appealed to my pocketbook. Appeasing the Monarchy would ensure money and influence, but it also appeared — for better or ill — that royalty was distant enough to take little interest in our experimentations unless they provided direct benefit to themselves, whereas the Separatists were interested in knowledge and were desperate to explore all scientific options available to them to turn the tide. However, their frail sensibilities would not so easily accept my experimentations.
IntroMartial-Monarchists.5.easy: But I must admit, the safety that the Monarchy gave was good for my money. Keeping the Monarchy happy would bring money and influence, and it also seemed, for better or worse, that the royal family was far enough away to not be very interested in our experiments, unless they helped the royals directly. The Separatists, on the other hand, were interested in knowledge and desperately wanted to try every scientific option they had to change the course of the war. But their sensitive feelings would not easily accept my experiments.
IntroMartial-Monarchists.5.short: Still, the Monarchy's safety appealed to my pocketbook. It offered money and influence, and took little interest in our experiments unless they served it. The Separatists hungered for any science that might turn the tide, but their delicate sensibilities would balk at mine.

IntroMartial-Monarchists.6.full: Ah, to be left to one's own devices or to be famously scrutinized, reviled, and revered in equal measure! The decision weighed upon me so heavily it gave me mild indigestion during my evening banquets. What direction should I choose to advance my most important scientific work?
IntroMartial-Monarchists.6.easy: Ah, to be left alone, or to be famous and watched, hated, and admired all at the same time! The decision was so heavy for me that it gave me a little stomach pain during my evening dinners. Which direction should I choose to move my most important scientific work forward?
IntroMartial-Monarchists.6.short: To be left alone, or to be scrutinized, reviled and revered! The choice gave me indigestion at dinner. Which way should my work go?

IntroMartial-Separatists.2.full: The length and difficulty of my journey was exacerbated by the ongoing conflict. Compounding this harried inconvenience, my spouse and I suffered the indignity of a lengthy interrogation by soldiers of the Separatist forces, who had imposed an unofficial martial government.
IntroMartial-Separatists.2.easy: My trip was even longer and harder because of the war. On top of this troublesome problem, my spouse and I had to accept the shame of a long questioning by soldiers of the Separatist forces, who had made an unofficial military government.
IntroMartial-Separatists.2.short: The war made my journey long and hard, and my spouse and I suffered a lengthy interrogation by the Separatists, who had imposed an unofficial martial government.

IntroMartial-Separatists.3.full: Peasants-turned-soldiers in their motley uniforms keep watch over the town from a newly erected outpost waving a sanguine flag. They spoke of freedom as they dug fresh graves in the cemetery; the wrought iron gates perpetually wreathed in lilies. I observed the daily horse-drawn carts, dragging the wounded towards ill-equipped infirmaries; my crimson reflection in the muddy ruts of unpaved highways.
IntroMartial-Separatists.3.easy: Farmers who had become soldiers, in their mixed uniforms, watch over the town from a new outpost, waving a blood-red flag. They spoke of freedom while they dug new graves in the cemetery, where the iron gates were always covered in lilies. Every day I saw carts pulled by horses, carrying the wounded to hospitals without enough equipment, and I saw my red reflection in the muddy tracks of the dirt roads.
IntroMartial-Separatists.3.short: Peasants-turned-soldiers watch the town from a new outpost under a blood-red flag, speaking of freedom as they dig fresh graves. Daily, carts drag the wounded to ill-equipped infirmaries through muddy roads.

IntroMartial-Separatists.4.full: It was both in spite of and because of this brashness that I found myself drawn to the scrappy Separatist upstarts and their eagerness to fight for the capricious whims of the great unwashed. The Separatists were desperate for the advantages that my family's experimentations provided, and while hesitant over our methods, were willing to further our knowledge in return. Unfortunately, this relationship made them more entitled to levy accusations towards us.
IntroMartial-Separatists.4.easy: Both in spite of and because of this boldness, I felt attracted to the young, fighting Separatists and their wish to fight for the changing moods of the poor masses. The Separatists desperately wanted the advantages that my family's experiments gave, and even though they were not sure about our methods, they were willing to help our knowledge grow in return. Sadly, this relationship also gave them more right to accuse us.
IntroMartial-Separatists.4.short: Despite, and because of, their brashness, I was drawn to the scrappy Separatists. They craved my family's experiments and, though wary of our methods, would further our knowledge in return. Sadly, this also entitled them to accuse us.

IntroMartial-Separatists.5.full: However, the influence of the throne was still absolute. If one could ingratiate themselves with the distracted Monarchy, their influence and money was on offer. The peasantry would be too discontent to focus on our more "ambitious" works. Unfortunately, unless experimentation directly benefited them, the Monarchy had no use for it.
IntroMartial-Separatists.5.easy: But the influence of the throne was still complete. If someone could win the favor of the distracted Monarchy, they could get its influence and money. The farmers would be too unhappy to pay attention to our more "ambitious" works. Sadly, the Monarchy had no use for experiments unless they helped it directly.
IntroMartial-Separatists.5.short: Yet the throne's influence was absolute, and its money and influence were there for those who won its favor, while the discontented peasants would ignore our more "ambitious" works. But the Monarchy valued experiments only if they served it.

IntroMartial-Separatists.6.full: Ah, to be left to one's own devices or to be famously scrutinized, reviled, and revered in equal measure! The decision weighed upon me so heavily that I could scarcely enjoy my afternoon pastries. Neither could the muffled wailing coming from the cellar laboratory nor the distant clattering of gunfire at night calm my weary mind. What direction should I choose to advance my most important scientific work?
IntroMartial-Separatists.6.easy: Ah, to be left alone, or to be famous and watched, hated, and admired all at the same time! The decision was so heavy for me that I could hardly enjoy my afternoon cakes. Neither the quiet crying from the laboratory in the cellar nor the far-away noise of guns at night could calm my tired mind. Which direction should I choose to move my most important scientific work forward?
IntroMartial-Separatists.6.short: To be left alone, or to be scrutinized, reviled and revered! I could scarcely enjoy my pastries; not even the muffled wailing from the cellar laboratory calmed me. Which way should my work go?

I am adamant in my disapproval of my father's hidden grudge against the current government and I offer them access to all goods within, free of charge. I am forever a proud citizen of this nation and harbor absolutely no ill-feelings, nor grudges which will spitefully fester in my psyche for the remainder of my years.

1stCrownCons.2.short: To be the **first** to draw the crown's ire was never my intent. The Queen had noticed my ambitions; the guards visited ever more often, their orange uniforms watching my hillside home.

1stCrownCons.3.full: How could I have been so bold? Why did they hound me so? It was enough to rattle the nerves to the point that I even found myself destroying the evidence of my work in a bout of mania. 1stCrownCons.3.easy: How could I have been so bold? Why did they follow me like this? It made me so nervous that I even destroyed the proof of my work in a moment of madness. But I continued, because I knew my mind was too strong to be held back! Watch me if you want, I will rise to fight again!
1stCrownCons.3.short: How could I be so bold? Their hounding so rattled me that I destroyed evidence of my work in a frenzy. But my intellect cannot be contained! I will rise to fight again!

ATOWSabotage1.2.easy: Nobody could change my mind. It was clear that my most moral and correct duty was to fight against tyranny in every form. The way this would be done made me shiver, but I knew from my own experience how strongly fear can motivate people.
ATOWSabotage1.2.short: I could not be swayed: my duty was to oppose tyranny. I shuddered at the means, but I knew how motivating fear can be.

ATOWSabotage1.4.full: The Barracks was a worthy target for my most righteous sabotage.

ATOWSabotageIntro1.3.short: For too long I had been ignored! What drives one to sabotage? Is it not enough to feel forgotten, downtrodden and spited by those who call you a colleague?

CommemorativeStatueEvent.2.full: While I shuddered at the thought of attracting too much attention to my activities in case they would be mistaken for deviance, I was unable to resist the gaze of noble adoration. With my frequent **visits to the Royal Advisor**, a rare - I struggle to say it - 'friendship' blossomed. With the regional influence wielded by the gentleman, he proposed a substantial gift in my honor - a statue at the center of a newly fashioned park within the city limits.
CommemorativeStatueEvent.2.easy: I was afraid of getting too much attention for my activities, in case people thought they were evil. But I could not resist the admiration of the nobles. Because of my many **visits to the Royal Advisor**, a rare, and it is hard for me to say it, 'friendship' grew. With the influence this man had in the region, he suggested a big gift in my honor: a statue in the middle of a new park in the city.
CommemorativeStatueEvent.2.short: Though wary of attention, I could not resist noble adoration. My frequent **visits to the Royal Advisor** grew into a rare 'friendship', and he proposed a gift in my honor: a statue at the heart of a new city park.

CommemorativeStatueEvent.3.full: Of course, this "gift" was not free. And with my cousins vying for similar attentions, it would require a bit of persuasion to receive this monument in my honor. The landmark meant little to me, of course, but to leave an indelible reminder of my family's bounteous contributions for all to see, that alone would provide me solace.
CommemorativeStatueEvent.3.easy: Of course, this "gift" was not free. And because my cousins wanted the same kind of attention, I would need to be a little convincing to get this monument in my honor. Of course, the monument itself did not mean much to me. But to leave a reminder that could never be removed, for everyone to see how much my family gave, that alone would comfort me.
CommemorativeStatueEvent.3.short: This "gift" was not free, and with my cousins vying for the same honor, persuasion would be needed. The statue meant little, but a lasting reminder of my family's contributions would comfort me.

CommemorativeSignIn.2.full: It was both a marvelous testament to the scientific spirit and a bitter eyesore sculpted from marred stone by amateur architects. My humility would not allow me to view it in a truly positive light. Yet, as frivolous as it was, it was vital in imprinting the legacy of my most revered family upon the region.
CommemorativeSignIn.2.easy: It was both a wonderful proof of the scientific spirit and an ugly sight, made from damaged stone by builders without skill. My modesty did not let me see it in a really positive way. But as silly as it was, it was very important for showing the legacy of my most respected family to the whole region.
CommemorativeSignIn.2.short: It was both a marvelous testament to science and an amateurish eyesore. My humility forbade admiring it, yet it was vital in imprinting my family's legacy on the region.

CommemorativeSignIn.3.full: **Which player visited the Commemorative Statue today?**

CommemorativeMAIN.2.full: Although the craftmanship was amateurish and the marble of lower grade than expected, I was once again stunned into silence as I arrived to marvel at the statue. What it lacked in polish, it excelled in artistic passion!
CommemorativeMAIN.2.easy: The work was not skilled, and the marble was not as good as I expected, but again I could not speak when I arrived and admired the statue. What it did not have in quality, it had in artistic passion!

CommemorativeMAIN.3.full: The picturesque monument always set my heart beating and drove me to tears. Sobbing into my handkerchief, I could feel the doubts melt away.
CommemorativeMAIN.3.easy: The beautiful monument always made my heart beat faster and made me cry. Crying into my handkerchief, I could feel my doubts melt away.

CommemorativeOTHER.2.full: How could they construct such a ghastly structure in the vague form of an unworthy clod? The thought set my features to crease into an ugly snear{0}
CommemorativeOTHER.2.easy: How could they build such a terrible thing in the unclear shape of a worthless fool? The thought made my face twist into an ugly look{0}

CommemorativeOTHER.3.full: And yet, set upon by the emotional heft of this abomination, I felt at once reinvigorated. For while love in its most passionate form was known to revive the soul, it is hate which raises the blood to the cheeks and sets the mind to precise action. I spoke a curse so vile I felt the lilacs wilt at the base of the wretched monument and spat upon the ground thrice.
CommemorativeOTHER.3.easy: And yet, when I felt the strong emotions of this horrible thing, I suddenly felt full of new energy. Because while love in its most passionate form can bring the soul back to life, it is hate that brings the blood to the cheeks and makes the mind act with precision. I said a curse so evil that I felt the lilacs at the bottom of the terrible monument become weak, and I spat on the ground three times.
CommemorativeOTHER.3.short: Yet the abomination reinvigorated me. Love may revive the soul, but hate sharpens the mind. I spoke a curse so vile the lilacs wilted, and spat on the ground thrice.

CommemorativeOTHER.4.full: My cousin may have enjoyed their victory in that moment, but soon I would be the one standing upon the pedestal... the pedestal of science!
CommemorativeOTHER.4.easy: My cousin may have enjoyed their victory in that moment, but soon I would be the one standing on the pedestal... the pedestal of science!

ATOW-FamineEvent.2.full: Because of the rapid expansion of war efforts, stocks of goods were increasingly hard to come by. When a famine struck in 1901, the food shortages caused mass riots. Ideas were thrown about for potential solutions - labor camps for dissidents, re-education facilities, pills that slow the metabolism - but all of these were bandages that did not address the root of the issue.
ATOW-FamineEvent.2.easy: Because the war grew so fast, it became harder and harder to get goods. When a famine came in 1901, the lack of food caused big riots. People suggested possible solutions: work camps for people against the government, places to teach people new opinions, pills that make the body use food more slowly. But all of these were only bandages that did not solve the real problem.
ATOW-FamineEvent.2.short: The war effort drained supplies, and when famine struck in 1901, food shortages sparked riots. Labor camps, re-education, metabolism pills: all mere bandages over the real problem.

ATOW-FamineEvent.3.full: While I offered it in jest at first, the most clean, efficient, and logical course was to utilize what we now had in droves to offset what we lacked. Were we to simply riddle our enemy's bodies with bullets and let them spoil the soil? Why should we allow perfectly good protein to waste away in the elements?
ATOW-FamineEvent.3.easy: At first I suggested it as a joke, but the cleanest, most efficient, and most logical solution was to use what we now had a lot of to make up for what we did not have. Should we just fill our enemies' bodies with bullets and let them rot in the soil? Why should we let perfectly good protein go to waste outside?
ATOW-FamineEvent.3.short: I suggested it in jest at first, but the cleanest, most logical course was to use what we had in abundance. Why let our enemies' bodies spoil the soil? Why waste perfectly good protein?

ATOW-FamineEvent.4.full: I decided to convene with my cousins and put the matter to a vote.
ATOW-FamineEvent.4.easy: I decided to meet with my cousins and let them vote on the matter.

ATOW-FamineEvent.5.full: We could continue to provide empty promises of more food in the future and preach hardiness and austerity. Or we could provide a **real**, sustainable solution that would guarantee success on the battlefield.
ATOW-FamineEvent.5.easy: We could continue to make empty promises of more food in the future and tell people to be strong and live simply. Or we could give a **real** solution that would last and make sure we win on the battlefield.

RoyalPriceisRight.2.full: With such direct access to royalty, it was mere weeks before I garnered a curious intrigue for my work. I knew this notoriety would serve my purposes well and shield me from scrutiny of my more unscrupulous designs.
RoyalPriceisRight.2.easy: With such direct access to the royal family, it took only a few weeks before people became curious about my work. I knew this fame would help my plans and protect me from people looking at my less honest projects.

RoyalPriceisRight.3.full: However, intrigue is what I desired. Suspicions, I did not. I aimed to remain like a whispering shadow, a ghostly hand so close as to curry favor and power, yet far enough removed to not arouse undesired attention. ATOW-End2.4.full: For while the world may have sped onward at a pace that our scientific contributions could not match, rendering our innovations lame and timid in comparison, I believe that my family's failure to make an impact on a world of the future is an important lesson. SeedResolution.2.full: I watched from my clandestine position as a singular corner in the secret laboratory became a storage place for various notes and torn pages from old manuscripts. With each passing evening, this obsessive collection of knowledge spilled onto the stone floors and tacked up on the walls like an artist's studio, spreading across the room like brown leaves on a brilliant vine. Such a wealth of knowledge, the likes of which I had never witnessed in all of my years at university.

Such a wealth of knowledge, more than I had ever seen in all my years at university.
SeedResolution.2.short: From hiding, I watched a corner of the secret laboratory fill with notes and torn manuscript pages, spilling onto the floor and up the walls like brown leaves on a vine. More knowledge than I had seen in all my years at university.
